case_name: LOTL PowerShell + Credential Theft + Lateral Movement
scenario_type: Suspicious PowerShell + Credential Theft + Lateral Movement
investigation_objective: Determine whether suspicious PowerShell execution on a finance workstation is benign activity, a false positive, or active credential theft and lateral movement requiring Tier 2 escalation.

likely_adversary_objective.summary: Credential Theft -> Privilege Escalation -> Lateral Movement -> Persistence

alerts.title: Suspicious Encoded PowerShell Execution
alerts.description: PowerShell executed with a Base64-encoded command from a Microsoft Word parent process.
evidence: Command line includes encoded command flag
Execution occurred in interactive user session
alerts.why_it_matters: Encoded PowerShell launched from Word is commonly associated with phishing payload execution and Living-off-the-Land attack behavior.

alerts.title: Impossible Travel Login
alerts.description: User authenticated from a Singapore IP address shortly after normal login activity from Virginia.
evidence: Travel time between locations is not physically possible
User has no historical login activity from Singapore
alerts.why_it_matters: This may indicate credential compromise or session hijacking.

alerts.title: MFA Failures Followed by Successful Login
alerts.description: Multiple MFA failures were followed by a successful authentication event.
evidence: No prior MFA failure pattern for this user
alerts.why_it_matters: Repeated MFA failures followed by success may indicate attacker persistence, MFA fatigue, or compromised authentication factors.

alerts.title: User Added to Domain Admins
alerts.description: User account was added to the Domain Admins group.
evidence: Change occurred shortly after anomalous login
alerts.why_it_matters: Unexpected privileged group membership is a major escalation indicator and increases blast radius.

alerts.title: LSASS Memory Access Attempt
alerts.description: Suspicious process attempted to access LSASS memory.
alerts.why_it_matters: Access to LSASS memory is commonly associated with credential dumping.

alerts.title: Rare Domain DNS Query
alerts.description: Host queried a rare external domain not previously seen in the environment.
evidence: Queried shortly after suspicious PowerShell execution
alerts.why_it_matters: Rare external domains following suspicious execution may indicate command-and-control activity.

alerts.title: Abnormal SMB Lateral Movement
alerts.description: User initiated SMB authentications to multiple internal servers within a short window.
evidence: User does not normally access these systems
alerts.why_it_matters: SMB fanout from a workstation after credential access activity may indicate lateral movement.

alerts.title: Remote Scheduled Task Created
alerts.description: A scheduled task was created remotely on an internal application server.
alerts.why_it_matters: Remote scheduled task creation is commonly used for persistence and remote execution.

threat_context.threat_summary: The observed chain maps to multiple MITRE ATT&CK tactics and resembles real attacker behavior: execution, privilege escalation, credential access, C2, lateral movement, and persistence.

observed_evidence: Word document launched from Downloads before PowerShell execution
User added to Domain Admins after anomalous authentication
SMB connections to APP-SRV-12, DB-SRV-03, and FS-SRV-08
Remote scheduled task created on APP-SRV-12

detection_recommendation.detection_goal: Detect encoded PowerShell launched from Microsoft Office followed by privileged account change, LSASS access, SMB lateral movement, or remote scheduled task creation within 30 minutes.

sigma_rule.title: Office Spawned Encoded PowerShell With Post-Execution Compromise Signals

tuning_recommendations: Suppress only when an approved change ticket or signed internal automation package is present.
Increase severity when user is newly added to a privileged group within 30 minutes.
